description: Desktop app to generate 3D models from images or prompt using local AI — runs entirely on your GPU

summary.one_liner: Modly is a desktop app that turns photos or prompts into 3D meshes using open source AI models that run locally on your GPU.
summary.what_it_does: Modly is a desktop application for Windows, Linux, and Apple Silicon macOS that performs image-to-3D mesh generation with open source models running locally. It has a node-based workflow editor (for example Image -> Generate Mesh -> Add to Scene) and a Models page for installing model and process extensions from GitHub repository URLs. Extensions can pull weights from Hugging Face, including multi-repository model sources, shared weight groups, and separately installable weight variants such as quantizations. Imported meshes can be smoothed and decimated in the app. A stdlib-only CLI (tools/modly-cli/agent.py) lets scripts and agents call a running Modly app for health checks, model listing, workflow runs, and mesh export.
use_cases: Turn a photo into a 3D model locally
Generate 3D meshes from images on a home GPU
Batch or scripted 3D generation via CLI
Install and manage open source image-to-3D models
notable: Runs open source image-to-3D models entirely on local GPU, with no cloud service described
Extension system: install model and process extensions from GitHub repo URLs via manifest.json
Weight variants let each quantization or precision be downloaded or deleted separately
AMD GPU support via ROCm on Linux and Windows, detected automatically
Stdlib-only CLI for agents and scripts to drive a running desktop app
caveats: Requires a capable GPU and Python environment setup for the backend
macOS support targets Apple Silicon only
Packaging for Apple Silicon uses a separate npm run package:mac step; installers are provided on the Releases page for Windows, Linux, and Apple Silicon macOS
keywords: run ai models on my gpu
